mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of CPIAUCSL (above 215) indicates elevated inflation that pressures real earnings growth and may prompt central bank rate hikes, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 215.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises by > 0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: The co-occurrence of low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.5) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 215) creates a 'stagflationary' environment that increases equity risk premiums and reduces forward returns, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5 and CPIAUCSL > 215.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a monthly decline in housing starts exceeding 0.5% signals weakening consumer demand and potential economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion periods, when HOUST falls by > 0.5% in 1 month, SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production exceeding 0.5% signals an immediate contraction in manufacturing output, which may trigger short-term equity selling pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls by > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts exceeding 0.5% indicates robust consumer spending on durable goods and housing, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises by > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate exceeding 2.0% indicates robust economic expansion that boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The co-occurrence of strong payroll growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) indicates a tight labor market that may fuel wage inflation and prompt aggressive monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in 1 month and UNRATE < 4.0%
failure_condition: When PAYEMS rises by > 0.5% in 1 month and UNRATE < 4.0%, SPX 20d returns are positive in > 60% of such periods.
